children: Nomura has reiterated its 'Buy' rating on Alibaba Group Holding with an unchanged target price of $178, expecting resilient ecommerce earnings despite macroeconomic pressures and robust growth in its cloud business as the company ramps up AI investments.

In its October 8 note, titled Stabilizing ecommerce profit; robust AI Cloud growth, Nomura said the trends highlighted in its October 2 report remained intact, providing Alibaba with "a solid profit pool to support its AI investments, which are emerging as a new growth driver".

For Alibaba Ecommerce Group (AEG), which includes traditional ecommerce and quick commerce (QC), Nomura expects customer management revenue (CMR) from China ecommerce to decline 5% year on year, in line with the latest Bloomberg consensus estimates. It estimates AEG's earnings before interest, taxes and amortisation (EBITA) at CNY 39.3 billion, above the consensus estimate of CNY 37 billion.

Within AEG, traditional ecommerce is estimated to have generated resilient EBITA of CNY 49 billion despite weak sales amid macroeconomic headwinds. Meanwhile, quick commerce losses are likely to have narrowed to CNY 10 billion in the September quarter from CNY 36 billion a year earlier.

Nomura believes Alibaba's ecommerce strategy has shifted towards "preserving cash flow rather than aggressively spending on subsidies to drive topline growth, including CMR, amid the current AI investment cycle".

Alibaba Cloud remains a bright spot, with revenue expected to grow 53% year on year, compared with the Street's consensus estimate of 50%. External cloud revenue growth is likely to have accelerated to 60% from 45% in the preceding quarter. Nomura estimates Alibaba Cloud's EBITA margin at 12%, compared with 11.6% in the June quarter.

Losses from AI Labs, which mainly comprises Qwen foundation models, AI applications and software-as-a-service (SaaS) products, are likely to have narrowed to CNY 11 billion in the September quarter from CNY 13.9 billion in the June quarter.
"With strong AliCloud profit growth, we expect the combined AliCloud and AI Labs businesses to reach breakeven in the upcoming December quarter," Nomura said.
Nomura forecasts consolidated revenue of CNY 272 billion, largely in line with consensus, and consolidated EBITA of CNY 30 billion, beating the Street's consensus estimate by 13%.
The brokerage's unchanged sum-of-the-parts (SOTP)-based target price of $178 implies 20 times estimated FY28 (calendar year 2027) price-to-earnings.

title: Alibaba: Nomura retains ‘Buy’, target price of $178 as AI cloud growth offsets ecommerce pressures
